clue.text: Rodent's limb cat is about to grab

indicators.note: the reversed cat takes hold of the limb, so the limb sits inside it
about here means turned round, so the word for a cat is read backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A cat is about to seize some animal's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Rodent' with the 's standing for 'is', a link; 'cat' looks like a predator after the rodent but only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmot is a large burrowing squirrel of mountain regions.

clue.text: A colour nearly used for suit

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the colour goes

parts.note: green is a colour

explanation.surface: A nearly-matching shade is chosen for a suit of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree with is to suit or be compatible with.

clue.text: It's expedient to create simple dress

parts.note: to make is to create
a shift is a plain straight dress

explanation.surface: Run up a simple dress, as the handy thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link: 'It's expedient' reads 'Expedient is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift serves as a temporary expedient.

clue.text: One's housed junior officer deprived of place in France

indicators.note: deprived of means losing the following part from the officer's title

parts.note: a lieutenant is a junior commissioned officer
lieu is French for place

explanation.surface: A young officer loses his posting in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is a person housed in rented property, an occupant.

clue.text: Mob's shifting alliance

indicators.note: shifting means changing position, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crowd's loyalties keep changing sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaille is a French-derived word for the rabble or riff-raff.

clue.text: Ideal place for castles in the air?

definitions.text: Ideal place for castles in the air?

parts.words: Ideal place for castles in the air?
parts.note: castles in the air are daydreams, so their home is an imaginary perfect realm high among the clouds

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Aristophanes means an absurdly idealised realm of fantasy.

clue.text: Failure to employ lower-class pundit

parts.note: non-U is British slang for not upper-class
a sage is a wise expert

explanation.surface: A working-class expert never finds a job.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were 1950s British labels for upper-class and other usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-usage is the lack of use of something.

clue.text: I reduced misery round house

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the misery word goes

parts.note: gloom is misery or despondency

explanation.surface: Someone lessens misery around the home.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a domed snow dwelling, circular in plan.

clue.text: Scraps with abandoned maidens, perhaps

parts.note: left means abandoned
a maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored

explanation.surface: Bits and pieces lying beside some abandoned young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maidens' are cricket overs in which no runs are scored, not young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftovers are scraps of food remaining after a meal.

clue.text: Divided up Japanese fencing, available in natural wood colour

indicators.note: fencing here means enclosing, so the brown colour surrounds the martial art

parts.note: brown is the colour of untreated wood
kendo is the Japanese sport of fencing with bamboo swords

explanation.surface: A Japanese sword sport, split up, sold in a natural brown finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' is used twice in effect: once in the name of the sport, and the sport then 'fences' it in. Here the second sense comes from the word 'fencing' as indicator, while 'Japanese fencing' gives KENDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something broken down into parts has been split or analysed into sections.

clue.text: Ride gives feeling of elation

definitions.meaning: a free ride in someone's car

explanation.definitionFit: Both a car journey offered free and an uplift in mood share the same short word.

clue.text: Thought about a second one before beginning to drink

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the last one

parts.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of the word drink

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about having one more before starting to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoned means worked out logically, as an adjective for a considered argument.

clue.text: Final instruction for beauty's toilette once? Exactly

definitions.text: Final instruction for beauty's toilette once?
definitions.meaning: the last step in an old-fashioned make-up routine was to put a beauty ... the face

explanation.definitionFit: Applying a beauty patch completes the look, and the same phrase means precisely right.

clue.text: One pound rejected in country using francs

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to lam is to beat or pound

explanation.surface: A single pound is turned down in a country using francs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali in West Africa uses the CFA franc as its currency.

clue.text: She takes a lot of trouble to compose her features

definitions.text: She takes a lot of trouble to compose her features

parts.words: She takes a lot of trouble to compose her features
parts.note: a newspaper columnist takes readers' troubles and writes feature columns, not someone making up her face

explanation.definitionFit: Advice columnists answer readers' problem letters in magazine features.

clue.text: Gun broken, relished using bare hands

indicators.note: a broken gun is in pieces, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: relished means loved or enjoyed

explanation.surface: With the gun out of action, someone enjoyed fighting barehanded.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungloved describes hands with no covering on them, i.e. bare.

clue.text: Where one drives to get such clothes, perhaps

definitions.text: Where one drives to get such clothes, perhaps

parts.words: Where one drives to get such clothes, perhaps
parts.note: a golfer drives the ball from a tee peg, and ready-made clothes are bought from a rail

explanation.definitionFit: Ready-to-wear clothing is bought ready-made rather than tailored.

clue.text: African country was to ban dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An African state was going to outlaw dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked nation of southern Africa.

clue.text: Solemn pronouncement in betting record that could pull punters in

indicators.note: in places the solemn pronouncement inside the betting record

parts.note: a bookmaker's book records bets
an oath is a solemn promise

explanation.surface: A vow written in a bookie's ledger could attract gamblers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punters' looks like gamblers, but means people in punts, flat river boats; a boat-hook pulls them in.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole with a hook used to draw small boats to the bank is this tool.

clue.text: Duke making heartless premier

indicators.note: heartless means losing the central letter of the word

parts.note: premier means first

explanation.surface: A duke is turning into a cruel prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' is slang for a hand clenched to fight ('put up your dukes'), not a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dukes is boxing slang for the hands rolled up to punch.

clue.text: One detects old magistrate's sound

indicators.note: sound means the noise made, so the word is identified by how it is said

parts.note: a censor was a magistrate in ancient Rome

explanation.surface: Someone picks up the noise an elderly magistrate makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensor is a device that detects heat, light or movement.

clue.text: Indirect route — the way one gets into security zone?

definitions.meaning: a road going round a town rather than through it

definitions.text: the way one gets into security zone?
definitions.meaning: entry to a guarded area is by showing a pass

explanation.definitionFit: A ring road skirting a town shares its name with gaining entry by a permit.

clue.text: Element offering new support for old craft

indicators.note: in a down entry, a support goes underneath, so the abbreviation for new comes after the ship

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A new prop is provided for an ancient vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble gas, a chemical element.

clue.text: For project, display too many pictures?

definitions.meaning: to stick out beyond what lies below
to hang too many paintings on a wall

explanation.surface: An exhibition organiser hangs far too many paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Jutting out beyond the base is the verb's sense; the other is a playful over-hanging of art.

clue.text: Fibre finally eaten only when cooked

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word eaten
cooked means altered, so the letters of only are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food is eaten at last only once it has been cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer spun into thread.

clue.text: It stops money being offered as bribe

definitions.meaning: a stopper for a cask or hole
British slang for a backhander or payoff

explanation.surface: A payment to buy silence stops the trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask stopper and British slang for a backhander share the same word.

clue.text: The first thing to stick in anyone's throat

definitions.text: The first thing to stick in anyone's throat

parts.words: The first thing to stick in anyone's throat
parts.note: the first man's fruit, said to have lodged in his throat, gives the name to the lump in every neck

explanation.definitionFit: The throat's laryngeal bulge is named from the forbidden fruit said to have caught in the first man's throat.

clue.text: One way and another, holding a level

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written
another way, here Rd, the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Two routes together keep a spirit level steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another way, giving RD, which 'holding' wraps round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a level of quality or attainment.

clue.text: Acting head, say, going into 4's payment

indicators.note: going into puts the abbreviation for say inside the payment

parts.note: the answer to 4 down is someone renting a home, and what they pay is rent
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A stand-in boss, for example, joins the lodger's rent payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules in place of a monarch who is too young or absent.
